notes.hybrid_rerank.hit_rate_at_5: MEASURED 2026-08-30 over all 235 ground-truth rows, k=5, zero degraded queries (evals/results/retrieval.md, ADR-001). This floor is LOW and deliberately not dressed up: the metric is single-positive and chunk-exact, so a neighbouring chunk carrying equally relevant prose scores as a total miss, and at 9168 chunks over 18 books near-misses are the common case. A diagnostic over 60 questions puts correct-book-in-top-5 at 0.650 and correct-section at 0.400, so retrieval has real signal that this number does not show. It is still the right metric to gate on, because every arm is penalised identically. Margin 0.01, not the usual noise-absorbing width, because this eval is DETERMINISTIC: no LLM in the measurement path and a fixed index, verified by two runs returning byte-identical metrics. There is no sampling noise to absorb, so anything beyond rounding is a real change. RE-MEASURE, do not hand-edit, if the corpus, the chunker, or evals/ground_truth.jsonl changes — all three move this number legitimately.
notes.hybrid_rerank.mrr_at_5: MEASURED 2026-08-30, same run and same caveats as hybrid_rerank.hit_rate_at_5. Worth reading alongside it: rerank lifts MRR (0.152 -> 0.167) while leaving hit-rate unchanged, which is the signature of a component that reorders a fixed candidate set and cannot surface a chunk fusion missed. If a future change moves hit-rate and MRR together, something other than the reranker did it. Margin 0.01 for the determinism reason above.
